formulas.title: Subject-Verb Agreement Rule
formulas.eq: Singular subject → singular verb; Plural subject → plural verb
formulas.note: The verb must always match the true grammatical subject, not any word that merely sits near it.

formulas.title: Basic Sentence Pattern (SVO)
formulas.note: This is the default word order for English declarative sentences; most errors involve disrupting this order incorrectly.

formulas.title: Comma Splice Fix Pattern
formulas.eq: Independent clause + [ , and/but/or/so ] + independent clause OR Independent clause + ; + independent clause
formulas.worked: Incorrect: "It was raining, we stayed inside." Correct: "It was raining, so we stayed inside." or "It was raining; we stayed inside."
formulas.note: A comma alone can never join two independent clauses — it needs a coordinating conjunction or must be replaced by a semicolon or period.

formulas.title: Parallel Structure Rule
formulas.eq: Item 1 (form X) + Item 2 (form X) + Item 3 (form X)
formulas.worked: Incorrect: "She likes swimming, to run, and biking." Correct: "She likes swimming, running, and biking."
formulas.note: All items joined in a list or comparison must share the same grammatical form (all -ing, all infinitives, etc.).

formulas.title: Relative Clause Attachment Rule
formulas.eq: Relative pronoun (who/which/that) immediately follows the noun it modifies
formulas.worked: Incorrect: "I saw a man's car who was tall." Correct: "I saw the car of a man who was tall."
formulas.note: Placing a relative clause far from its intended noun creates a misplaced-modifier style ambiguity.

formulas.title: Tense Backshift Rule (Reported Speech)
formulas.worked: Direct: "I am tired," she said. Reported: She said (that) she was tired.
formulas.note: When the reporting verb is in the past tense, the tense of the original statement typically shifts one step back.

formulas.title: Apostrophe Possession Rule
formulas.eq: Singular noun + 's; Plural noun ending in s + s'
formulas.worked: "the girl's book" (one girl) vs. "the girls' book" (multiple girls)
formulas.note: The position of the apostrophe relative to the s is what distinguishes singular from plural possession in writing.

formulas.title: Coordinating Conjunction Comma Rule
formulas.worked: "I wanted to go, but it was raining."
formulas.note: FANBOYS (for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so) joining two full independent clauses is preceded by a comma.

formulas.title: Either/Or, Neither/Nor Agreement Rule
formulas.eq: Verb agrees with the subject NEAREST to it
formulas.worked: "Neither the manager nor the employees were available." (verb agrees with "employees")
formulas.note: This is one of the most commonly misapplied concord rules in formal writing and exams.

formulas.title: Modifier Placement Rule
formulas.eq: Modifier should sit directly next to the word it is intended to describe
formulas.worked: Incorrect: "Running quickly, the finish line was reached." Correct: "Running quickly, she reached the finish line."
formulas.note: A dangling or misplaced modifier attaches itself, by position, to the wrong (or no) noun in the sentence.
